article_title: CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education
citation: Agerri, R., Aldabe, I., Cabrio, E., Cieliebak, M., Deriu, J., Flores, M., Kapočiūtė-Dzikienė, J., Kuizinienė, D., Rico, A., Ruiz-González, A., Soroa, A., Vaškevičius, M. and Villata, S. (2026). CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education. SEPLN 2026. https://www.hitz.eus/critics
title: Corpus of 500 annotated competency-based assessments in higher education for developing and evaluating the Teacher Evaluator
description: The project will compile and annotate 500 competency-based assessments in higher education, consisting of "questionnaires with student responses and corresponding teacher's assessments" available in-house at UPV/EHU. This dataset will be the basis for developing and evaluating the Teacher Evaluator tool and research in WP4. WP2 will annotate argumentation graphs, critical questions, and feedback/assessment for benchmarking, and the data will be anonymized and released following privacy and open science policies.
requirements: manual annotation of argumentation graphs, critical questions, and feedback/assessment
constraints: data are in-house at UPV/EHU and pertain to higher education
examples: WP2 will also derive new instruction and alignment datasets from already instructed models using the magpie approach to reduce the need for expensive human-annotated instruction data.

article_title: A Systematic Review of Empirical Research on Graphing Numerical Data in K-12 STEM Education
citation: Verena Rufai, Dominik Thüsbj, Sarah Malonecj, Stefan Küchemanndi, Sebastian Becker-Genschowe, Markus Vogelf, Roland Brünkengj, Jochen Kuhnhi. (2024). A Systematic Review of Empirical Research on Graphing Numerical Data in K-12 STEM Education. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED
title: Corpus of 50 peer-reviewed empirical studies on graphing in K-12 STEM education
description: The review assembles a corpus of 50 peer-reviewed empirical studies on graphing in K-12 STEM education identified in SCOPUS, ERIC, and PsychInfo using PRISMA-guided screening with ASReview and Rayyan. The studies were published between 1979 and 2024, with publication rates peaking around 2019 and 2020. Most studies were conducted in the USA, followed by Indonesia and Australia. Participant numbers ranged from three to 745, averaging 116 students (SD = 174), and most studies involved high school students (n=43).
requirements: Included studies examined self-generated or partially completed, convention-based graphical representations constructed from numerical data by K-12 students in STEM contexts.
constraints: Studies investigating graphing based on given verbal-textual or mathematical-symbolical information, function graphs not based on data, and pure graph interpretation of provided graphs were excluded.
key_sources: Verena Rufai, Dominik Thüsbj, Sarah Malonecj, Stefan Küchemanndi, Sebastian Becker-Genschowe, Markus Vogelf, Roland Brünkengj, Jochen Kuhnhi. (2024). A Systematic Review of Empirical Research on Graphing Numerical Data in K-12 STEM Education. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED

article_title: Strategies Training in the Teaching of Reading Comprehension for EFL Learners in Indonesia
citation: Junaidi Mistar, Alfan Zuhairi & Nofita Yanti. (2016). Strategies Training in the Teaching of Reading Comprehension for EFL Learners in Indonesia. English Language Teaching, 9(2). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v9n2p49
title: Researcher-made 50-item multiple-choice test of literal and inferential reading comprehension
description: A researcher-developed multiple-choice instrument used to measure the treatment effect after the twelve training sessions. It "contained 50 items, consisting of 30 items of literal comprehension and 20 items of inferential comprehension", was tried out for difficulty, discriminating power, and distracter effectiveness, and showed a Kuder-Richardson 20 internal-consistency reliability index of 0.74, which the authors judged highly reliable for research purposes.
requirements: Prior try-out for difficulty level, discriminating power, and effectiveness of distracters
constraints: Reliability index of 0.74 as printed by the authors
examples: Administered at the end of the training sessions to both groups, with scores analysed via ANCOVA using the mid-semester teacher-made test as covariate
key_sources: Junaidi Mistar, Alfan Zuhairi & Nofita Yanti. (2016). Strategies Training in the Teaching of Reading Comprehension for EFL Learners in Indonesia. English Language Teaching, 9(2). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v9n2p49
